headline: Rock Legend Honored as Scientists Name New Snake After Slash
meta_description: Scientists in Papua New Guinea discovered a new reddish-brown snake and named it Lielaphis slashi to honor Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash for his lifelong advoc…
summary_short: A newly identified nocturnal groundsnake from Papua New Guinea has been named after Slash of Guns N' Roses, honoring his decades of support for herpetology and conservat…
body:
Scientists have formally described a new species of nocturnal groundsnake from the forests of Papua New Guinea and named it Lielaphis slashi—in honor of Saul Hudson, professionally known as Slash, the lead guitarist of Guns N' Roses, for his lifelong promotion and advocacy of snakes, zoos, and museums. The reddish-brown, unmarked snake represents the twentieth confirmed species within the genus Lielaphis, a group found primarily on New Guinea island. "As a long-time herpephile, I am extremely honored and humbled to have Lielaphis slashi from New Guinea named after me," Slash said in response to the naming. "It is really exciting, I never would have imagined this moment would arrive."

Christopher Austin, professor of natural science and curator of amphibians and reptiles at Louisiana State University, first discovered specimens of the snake in July 2006 in a secondary forest in Sandaun Province. What he initially thought was a previously known species was later confirmed through genetic analysis and detailed comparison of scales and morphology to be entirely new to science. The challenge lies in the groundsnakes' secretive nocturnal habits and highly similar appearance—so much so that the New Guinea species are difficult to distinguish without close examination, leaving researchers convinced many more undescribed species await discovery in the region.

The discovery carries urgency. New Guinea, widely recognized as a biologically diverse hotspot, faces immediate threats from timber harvesting, industrial plantations, coffee farming, and mining operations. Sara Ruane, the Field Museum's Associate Curator of Herpetology, emphasized that describing these species is crucial precisely because their habitats are disappearing. The formal identification of Slash's groundsnake underscores both the richness of New Guinea's wildlife and the pressing need to document and protect it before species vanish unnamed into extinction.
quick_facts: New nocturnal snake from Papua New Guinea named Lielaphis slashi
Twentieth species confirmed in the Lielaphis groundsnake genus
Discovered July 2006 in Sandaun Province secondary forest
Named to honor Slash's decades of snake and zoo advocacy
New Guinea habitats threatened by mining and coffee farming
